limitations: The win-probability model is slightly overconfident in the extreme tails (in the 80–90% bin the model predicts 85% but teams won 81%).

Pressure-specific skill is only moderately repeatable (held-out correlation roughly 0.2 for bowlers and 0.4 for batters), so ranks 6–10 in each list are not statistically separable; see the rank-range and P(top 10) columns.
Blend weights were estimated on the same random match splits used to evaluate them, so the held-out correlations are mildly optimistic.
Ratings are runs-based. Fielding, captaincy and the non-striker's contribution are not modelled, and run-outs are charged to neither bowler nor non-striker.

The 'T20' group in the data pack contains IPL plus two A-team events; IPL-only checks use IPL fixtures only. T20I opposition varies in strength and is only partly handled by the joint batter-bowler model.
No pitch, venue, injury or auction-availability information was used. IPL 2027 retentions and the final auction pool were not known when this was built.
Ball-level R² is tiny by nature (cricket outcomes are noisy); player-level repeatability across match splits is the metric that matters.

Domestic (Indian) list: nationality comes from India / India A entries in the data pack's team mapping. IPL players with no national-team entry were classified from public records and flagged in the data (nationalitySource); a few overseas players without an entry were excluded by name. Uncapped Indian players outside the IPL and the listed events are not covered.
